title: Aurora Financial - cost savings playbook (Optimize pilot)
content:
Purpose
-----
Notes and working calculations for the Aurora Financial Redwood Optimize pilot. Goal: show a concrete before/after cost and latency picture for the Aurora production traffic shape, plus an actionable rollout plan for the recommended optimizations. This is a working doc — rough numbers flagged below.

Customer context
---------------
- Customer: Aurora Financial (internal alias: aurora-fin)
- Workload: customer-facing knowledge assistant + document summarization. Production traffic is predominantly short-chat queries (avg 120 tokens generated), with a smaller tail of long summarization jobs (avg 2,400 tokens).
- Current deployment: hosted API using model X-large (unquantized 16-bit), default routing to us-west region. No prefix caching. Conservative batching settings (batch size cap = 4, latency SLO 300ms p95 for chat).
- Baseline monthly metrics (observed Feb):
  - Monthly requests: ~85k requests
  - Generated tokens per month: 32.4M tokens
  - Average response latency (p95): 320ms for chat, 1.6s for long summaries
  - Billable host compute (approx): 6,500 GPU-hours / month
  - Monthly spend (hosted inference + infra): $84,200 (compute $69k, network & infra $6.2k, support/overheads $9k)

Optimization recommendations summary (from Redwood Optimize)
---------------------------------------------------------
1) Quantize model to q4_0 variant (maintain output quality via eval set)
2) Enable prefix KV caching for repeat prompt prefixes (knowledge assistant)
3) Increase per-GPU batching window modestly + adaptive batching (reduce cold waits)
4) Route long summarization jobs to a cost-optimized model-slice (same family, lower memory footprint) when latency budget is >1s
5) Apply token-level attention trimming for very long summaries (truncate low-value context after 4k)
6) Slight prompt engineering: move static system context to cached prefix to avoid re-tokenizing on every request

Before/After high-level numbers (modelled)
----------------------------------------
- Key assumptions used in calculations:
  - q4 quantization reduces GPU compute cost per token by ~58% for generation workloads in our benchmarks (family-dependent). We conservatively model 50% compute cost reduction to account for Aurora-specific prompt shapes.
  - Prefix caching will reduce average compute work for chat sessions by 18% (sessions with repeated system text and long-lived KV cache).
  - Improved batching and adaptive window reduces per-token overhead by another ~12% across all request types.
  - Routing long summaries to a smaller variant lowers cost on those requests by 65% but increases avg latency for that cohort by ~0.7s (still within customer SLAs for non-interactive jobs).

Modeled monthly cost (rounded)
- Baseline (observed): $84,200
  - Compute: $69,000
  - Networking/infra/overhead: $15,200
- After Optimize recommendations (projected): $29,700
  - Compute: $20,300 (net reduction driven by quantization + batching + caching)
  - Networking/infra/overhead: $9,400 (smaller because routing reduces cross-zone traffic and fewer retries/errors expected)
- Projected absolute savings: $54,500 / month 
- Projected percent savings: 64.7% monthly

Detailed compute breakdown (estimates)
- Baseline compute hours: 6,500 GPU-hours/mo (mix of A100/V100-equivalent pricing in our internal model)
- Post-optimization compute hours: 2,200 GPU-hours/mo (quantization + batching reduce effective GPU-hours)
- Notes: these numbers come from applying the per-token speedups benchmarked in the Optimize telemetry dataset and scaling by Aurora's token distribution. We left a 15% safety margin baked into the predicted reduction.

Quality & latency tradeoffs
--------------------------
- Expected quality delta: null to -0.6% on Aurora's eval set for chat behavior (within the customer acceptance threshold). We validated 120 sample prompts from Aurora's pAIset — minimal differences in user-facing correctness.
- Latency: interactive p95 should remain near or under 350ms after tuning (marginal change vs baseline). The long-summary cohort will see p95 increase up to ~2.4s in our routing scenario (acceptable for batch summaries).
- Risk: rare prompt constructs where quantization amplifies hallucination risk — flagging these in the eval harness with regression alerts.

Customer-facing one-pager numbers (for sales/CS)
------------------------------------------------
- Current monthly bill estimate: $84k
- Redwood Optimize recommended changes: quantization + caching + smarter routing + batching
- Estimated new monthly bill: $30k (approx)
- Net savings: ~$54.5k / month (~65% cost reduction)
- Implementation effort (Rough): 2-3 sprint weeks to change config + monitor + one small prompt engineering pass; no model retrain required.

Short worked example (per-request)
--------------------------------
- Baseline: average chat request = 120 generated tokens, effective GPU cost per token = $0.0018 (derived from baseline), per-request compute cost = $0.216
- After quantize+batch+cache: effective GPU cost per token = $0.00062, per-request compute cost = $0.0744
- Per-request saving = $0.1416 (~66% lower)
- Multiply by 85k requests/mo => compute savings ~ $12k/mo just from chat cohort; additional savings from long summaries compound to reach the total modeled number.

Assumptions & caveats (call out)
--------------------------------
- Model family: recommendations are family-specific. The q4 speedups are validated on the same architecture Aurora uses; if Aurora swaps to a different model family, numbers must be re-run.
- Traffic variance: numbers extrapolated from Feb usage; seasonality could move totals +/- 20%.
- Implementation risk: prefix caching requires safe cache eviction policies; misconfiguration could leak PII. We must apply strict scoping and test harnesses.
- Billing model: we assumed hosted inference + infra pricing; if Aurora moves to Dedicated or Private, margin/discounts change the savings profile.

Proposed rollout plan (minimal risk)
-----------------------------------
1) Preflight (1 week): create a canary project with same traffic replay using recorded traces (oblivious to PII), run Optimize bench to validate q4 throughput and quality on Aurora eval set. Owner: Ethan. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-2413.
2) Config changes (1 sprint week): enable q4 variant + adaptive batching + prefix caching for 10% of traffic. Closely monitor regression alerts and p95 latencies. Owner: Lin.
3) Canary evaluation (2 weeks): validate model output quality, p95, error rate, and infra metrics. If regression > 1% on key eval prompts, rollback or tweak quantization config.
4) Ramp (2–4 weeks): 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with staged rollout and automated rollback on SLO violation. Owner: Priya.
5) Post-mortem and docs (1 week): produce customer-facing report and update Aurora runbook and SLO thresholds.

Monitoring & key metrics to track
--------------------------------
- Monthly spend by cost center (compute / infra / networking)
- Per-request compute cost (moving average)
- p95 latency (chat) and p95 latency (summaries)
- Output regression rate on Aurora eval set (daily)
- Cache hit rate for prefix caching
- Batching utilization and median batch size

Open questions / action items
---------------------------
- [ ] Confirm model family & exact model id Aurora is willing to run quantized (question for CS).
- [ ] Get Aurora approval on allowed latency bump for summarization jobs.
- [ ] Security review for prefix cache content (Lin).
- [ ] Owner for instrumentation changes to surface compute cost per request in Aurora dashboard (Priya).
- [ ] Link to replay traces for canary: insert drive link here once sanitized.

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (sensitivity of monthly savings to variation in key levers)
- If quantization effectiveness is 40% vs the modeled 50% => projected savings ~48% (approx $40k/mo).
- If batch improvements only yield 6% instead of 12% => projected savings ~55% (approx $46k/mo).
- If traffic increases 25% => absolute $ savings rise but percent savings roughly similar (since optimizations scale).

Notes to self
------------
- Keep the customer-facing one-pager short and use the $30k new bill headline; CS wants a conservative number for the exec.
- Add a small visual chart (before/after stacked bars) in the final spreadsheet.

References
---------
- Cost model spreadsheet (working): https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AuroraCostModel
- Optimize telemetry benchmark used: internal bench id: bench-q4-2025-01
- PR for batching runtime improvements: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/782
